newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks higher on electronics in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks higher on electronics in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices edged higher in late trade on Tuesday on relatively strong electronics shares and Monday's confidence-boosting statement by the central bank, brokers said.
With 35 minutes left, the benchmark stock index had risen 15.98 points or 0.19 percent to 8,437.85.
Turnover was an active T$75.74 billion.
Electronics shares had risen 1.69 percent while electricals had advanced 1.07 percent.
Brokers said trading was dull due to a lack of market-inspiring factors.
"Were it not for the relatively strong performance of electronics, profit-taking from Monday's gains would have dragged down the index," said George Hou, a fund manager of Jardine Fleming.
Share prices ended sharply up on Monday, soaring 119.62 points or 1.44 percent to 8,421.87.
Motherboard maker Asustek rose by the daily seven-percent limit to T$791. Computer part maker Compeg had also soared to its limit, rising T$12 to T$186.

Brokers said the market also gained support from a statement by deputy central bank governor Hsu Chia-tung on Monday that the bank, which has tried to cool the island's recent bourse fever, would like to see "appropriate" growth.
